data.headline: S&P 500 futures funds trim net shorts as asset managers pare longs
data.summary: The November 17 CFTC report shows two groups moving closer together. Leveraged funds reduced their net short by 68,082 E-mini S&P 500 contracts over the week. Asset managers cut their net long by 19,081.

bull.text: Leveraged funds were net short 234,978 contracts on November 17, down from 303,060 on November 10. Their position remained net short after the reduction.

bear.text: Asset managers’ net long fell from 914,130 to 895,049 contracts. Their smaller position tempers the more constructive reading from leveraged funds.

watch.text: Open interest rose to 2,096,958 contracts from 2,017,687. The next weekly report can show whether participation keeps growing as the groups adjust their positions.

limitations: E-mini S&P 500 futures are a proxy for SPY exposure. Weekly positions can include hedges. This report supplies no current SPY options-chain or dealer-gamma measurement.

sources.title: CFTC · E-MINI S&P 500 - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE · 2026-11-17
